root_idea.summary: A semantic core of slipping, moving away from stability, or failing to remain firm.
root_idea.development: The physical loss of footing extends to the sun's decline, arguments becoming invalid or being rebutted, and persons being overcome or brought to loss.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form IV perfect citation form أَدْحَضَ.
Displayed under the singular active-participle citation form دَاحِضٌ.
Displayed under the singular passive-participle citation form مُدْحَضٌ; the Quran occurrence is its plural form.

senses.definition: To rebut, invalidate, or render null.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction لِيُدْحِضُوا بِهِ الْحَقَّ, the verb denotes using something to rebut or invalidate the truth; this is the figurative argumentative use of the causative Form IV.
Used of an argument, plea, allegation, or evidence; in the Quranic occurrence, it predicates that the opponents' argument lacks validity or has been refuted.

senses.definition: Made to slip; overcome or defeated.
senses.usage_conditions: Passive result of Form IV, describing those brought into loss or defeat; the Quranic occurrence uses the plural form مُدْحَضِينَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slip or lose one's footing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The basic intransitive physical use, said of a foot and also of a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the sun, to decline from the meridian toward the place of setting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of physical slipping or movement away from a stable position.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause a foot or person to slip; of rain, to make a place slippery.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The physical causative use of Form IV, distinct from its Quranic figurative use of rebutting or invalidating.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slippery place; also water that causes slipping.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete noun for a place or substance associated with loss of footing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lacking firmness, stability, determination, or resolve in affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative idiomatic use associated with the expression دُحْضُ الأَقْدَامِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cause or place of slipping; a place where feet do not remain firm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place or circumstance liable to cause loss of footing; synonymous with مَزَلَّةٌ in the cited usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place in which one slips often or repeatedly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive designation for a frequently slippery place.

The supplied lexical evidence directly describes the Form IV causative action. The gloss “the losers” for مُدْحَضِينَ is contextual support for its passive result, not an independent lexical source.
